correctness.rationale: For \(p=kd+1\), translation shift S is one characteristic-p Jordan block; its difference \(Z=S-I\) is nilpotent of length p. The first nonconstant nonzero coefficient of the adjacency connection polynomial at \(S=I\) is exactly degree d: lower binomial moments vanish by subgroup root-of-unity orthogonality, and \(c_d=d/d!\) is nonzero. Thus \(A-dI=Z^dU(Z)\), U(0) nonzero, so Jordan blocks have sizes k+1 once and k (d-1) times. The Frobenius identity \(A^p=dI\) and exact kernel of \(A^t-I\) (dimension 0, d, or p) prove the orbit census. Matrix-rank, subgroup-moment and exhaustive-state programs were replayed from actual package files; finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural infinite-family classification of synchronous linear dynamics on connected highly symmetric cyclotomic graphs. The index k and degree d determine a singular long Jordan chain, the exact permutation order and all orbits; this exposes a structurally meaningful discontinuity between modular (nonsemisimple) dynamics and characteristic-zero spectral information. It includes noncycle graphs (e.g. p=13,k=3,d=4), arbitrary higher cyclotomic indices, and every finite state-field extension; it is not a one-off finite numerical invariant.
